The arc closes: examples/sph_fluid_2d ported the algorithm to a CPU //! loop because the GL backend had no compute. This is the same paper running //! where it belongs - eleven kompute kernels (sort_kernels.zig), each //! translated once to its own WGSL module (spv2wgsl --entry, the multi-kernel //! path), dispatched through ONE `z.Compute` pipe, rendered zero-copy by //! `z.FluidDiscs` straight from the compute storage buffer. //! Positions never visit the CPU. //! //! Per substep: gravityMouse -> viscosity -> predict -> [counting sort: //! clearGrid -> countGrid -> prefixSum -> scatter -> copyback] -> density -> force //! -> applyAndFinalize, then one instanced draw of N SDF discs coloured by //! density. The sort reorders pos/vel/prev into cell order so the neighbour //! passes read contiguous (coalesced) memory - ~3x the per-particle grid. //! //! Controls: drag = push, shift+drag (or the attract toggle) = pull; sliders //! for the paper's four knobs; reset = re-spawn the centre disk. const std = @import("std"); const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator; const z = @import("zimr"); const zm = @import("zm"); const float64 = zm.float64; const float = zm.float; const Vec2 = zm.Vec2; const clamp = zm.clamp; const length = zm.length; const splat2 = zm.splat2; const fk = @import("sort_kernels.zig"); const atkinson_mono_ttf = @embedFile("atkinson_mono_ttf"); /// The per-kernel WGSL table, built straight from the kernel manifest /// (`fk.kernels`) - one `@embedFile` per entry, no hand-kept list to drift out /// of sync with the kernel file. Each `<name>_wgsl` module is generated by the /// build's compute pipeline (`spv2wgsl --entry <name>` over the one SPIR-V /// module). A name in `fk.kernels` with no generated module is a compile error /// right at the `@embedFile` below - exactly the drift we want caught at build /// time rather than as a runtime "kernel not registered". const Pipe = z.Compute(fk); const kernel_wgsls: [fk.kernels.len]Pipe.KernelWgsl = blk: { var arr: [fk.kernels.len]Pipe.KernelWgsl = undefined; for (fk.kernels, 0..) |name, i| { arr[i] = .{ .name = name, .wgsl = @embedFile(name ++ "_wgsl") }; } break :blk arr; }; const substeps: u32 = 1; // THE DEFAULTS, IN ONE PLACE. These must equal the `State` field initialisers below (this // Zig cannot read struct defaults reflectively, and `State{}` is not constructible because // `font` has none). They are also `fluid_gpu`'s values - that is what makes the two demos a // controlled comparison. The DEFAULTS button restores them and the diagnostics panel names // any knob that has drifted off them. const def_g_force: f32 = 0.0099; // x 9.8 m/s^2 == fluid_gpu's flat gravity_y of 0.097 const def_rest_density: f32 = 15.39; const def_visc_beta: f32 = 0.017; const def_k_far: f32 = 0.009; const def_k_near: f32 = 0.028; const def_wall_normal: f32 = 1.0; const def_wall_tangent: f32 = 0.0; const def_mouse_force: f32 = 3.0; const def_phone_gravity: bool = false; /// Sim-pixel radius of a rendered disc (the reference's RENDER_RADIUS). const mouse_radius: f32 = 90.0; const State = struct { font: z.Font, pipe: z.Compute(fk), /// THE SAME KERNELS, RUN AS PLAIN ZIG. kompute compiles one source for two targets, so /// this is the only way to ask "is the transpiler lying?" about the PHYSICS kernels. /// `sort_smoke` proved the sort and the neighbour walk are bit-correct on the GPU - it /// never tested density/force/apply. Toggle this on at a low particle count: if the /// fluid pools on the CPU and sprays on the GPU, the fault is in the toolchain, and the /// kernel that differs is the one to look at. cpu_pipe: z.Compute(fk), cpu_sim: bool = false, discs: z.FluidDiscs, ui_host: z.UiHost, /// Persistent spawn/reset scratch (reset re-seeds through the same /// upload path; 20k x 8B is cheap to keep). scratch: []Vec2, // The paper's knobs (uploaded into Params each frame). k_far: f32 = def_k_far, k_near: f32 = def_k_near, // rho 0, the rest/desired density: pressure is k_far*(rho - rho 0). Higher = the // fluid wants to pack denser (more cohesive); lower = it expands. rest_density: f32 = def_rest_density, /// One gain mapping the phone's effective gravity (m/s^2, from the /// accelerometer) -> sim acceleration. ~0.01 reproduces "normal" gravity held /// upright; this is DOUBLE that, for a punchier default. With phone gravity /// off it just scales the straight-down 1g fallback. /// MATCHED TO `fluid_gpu`, which applies a flat `gravity_y = 0.097`. Here gravity is a /// SCALE on the device's 9.8 m/s^2 vector, so the same downward acceleration needs /// 0.097 / 9.8 = 0.0099. (At the old 0.02 this demo pulled twice as hard as the other.) g_force: f32 = def_g_force, /// On -> gravity comes from the phone's proper-acceleration vector: tilt steers /// it, shaking sloshes it, flat = float (zero-g), free-fall = weightless. Off /// -> plain straight-down gravity. Needs an https/localhost origin for sensor /// data (else it falls back to straight down regardless). /// OFF by default, to match `fluid_gpu`, which uses a flat constant gravity. /// /// With this ON, gravity comes from the ACCELEROMETER - and `getDeviceGravity` maps /// only the x,y components into the canvas plane, so a phone held flat (or just tilted /// back to read) has almost no in-plane gravity: the fluid is in FREE FALL and expands /// to fill the box with no free surface. That is the feature working correctly, but it /// made the demo look catastrophically broken next to `fluid_gpu` and sent a long hunt /// after a physics bug that did not exist. Tilt-gravity is a great demo - it just /// cannot be the DEFAULT when this example's whole purpose is to be a controlled /// comparison against a constant-gravity twin. phone_gravity: bool = def_phone_gravity, /// Wall-contact damping (proportion of velocity removed at the boundary). /// normal_damp = into-wall component (1.0 = fully inelastic, the realistic /// default); tangent_damp = along-wall friction - kept at 0 now that the /// co-location shear (the real cause of the corner jets) is fixed, so the /// walls are frictionless and the fix stands on its own. Crank it to compare. wall_normal_damp: f32 = def_wall_normal, wall_tangent_damp: f32 = def_wall_tangent, visc_beta: f32 = def_visc_beta, mouse_force_mag: f32 = def_mouse_force, attract_toggle: bool = false, paused: bool = false, /// Batch every substep's dispatches into ONE compute pass / submit /// (vs a submit per dispatch). On by default - fewer submits is faster. batch_mode: bool = true, /// How many particles to DRAW (the sim always runs the full count). Below /// the max this shows the first-N in cell order - i.e. the top rows, since /// the sort puts the lowest-numbered cells first. Handy for eyeballing the /// sort, not a perf knob. sim_count_f: f32 = 20000, adapter_buf: [192]u8 = undefined, adapter_len: usize = 0, en_gravity: bool = true, en_grid: bool = true, en_viscosity: bool = true, en_predict: bool = true, en_density: bool = true, // One-shot: prime the counting sort (build cell_start + sort the spawn // layout) before the first substep, so frame 1's viscosity reads a valid // grid instead of an uninitialised one. sort_primed: bool = false, en_force: bool = true, en_apply: bool = true, /// DIAGNOSTIC PROBE (temporary): particle 0's position and the bbox of all of them, /// read back unconditionally. The discs render nothing while the sim reports 8 ms/sub, /// so the one question worth answering is whether the POSITIONS are sane. If they are, /// the compute is fine and the disc pipeline is at fault; if they are NaN or collapsed, /// it is the other way round. probe_p0: Vec2 = .{ 0, 0 }, probe_min: Vec2 = .{ 0, 0 }, probe_max: Vec2 = .{ 0, 0 }, probe_nan: u32 = 0, /// The effective gravity handed to the kernels this frame (see the diagnostics panel). dbg_gravity: Vec2 = .{ 0, 0 }, probe_pos1: Vec2 = .{ 0, 0 }, /// RAW first entries of each buffer. Statistics have now sent me down three dead /// ends; the actual bytes will not. probe_gc: [4]u32 = .{ 0, 0, 0, 0 }, probe_cs: [4]u32 = .{ 0, 0, 0, 0 }, probe_den: Vec2 = .{ 0, 0 }, probe_pos2: Vec2 = .{ 0, 0 }, /// How many Params fields the SHADER disagrees with the HOST about, and the name of the /// first one. Three of twenty have ever been verified; this checks all of them. param_bad: u32 = 0, param_first: []const u8 = "-", param_host: f32 = 0, param_gpu: f32 = 0, stat_rho: f32 = 0, /// Mean rho_near. When `rho` sits BELOW rest density the far-pressure term is /// ATTRACTIVE, so the near term is the only thing left that can hold the fluid open - /// which makes this the number that decides whether the expansion is even physical. stat_rho_near: f32 = 0, stat_frozen_pct: f32 = 0, // Grid occupancy (from grid_counts readback, diagnostics only): the // fullest cell, the mean over non-empty cells, and how many cells exceed // the old max_per_cell figure. The counting sort is UNCAPPED, so this no // longer means dropped neighbours - it's just a density gauge for tuning. stat_cell_max: u32 = 0, stat_cell_avg: f32 = 0, stat_cells_capped: u32 = 0, frame_no: u32 = 0, prev_stat_pos: []Vec2, // ---- Average-FPS benchmark readout (the baseline-to-beat) ---- // A STABLE windowed average recomputed every `fps_window_secs` so the // displayed value doesn't jitter while you read it; accum/frames build the // next window. fps_avg: f32 = 0, // published windowed average (the headline number) fps_accum_time: f32 = 0, // seconds accumulated in the current window fps_accum_frames: u32 = 0, // ---- Vsync-independent benchmark ---- // Run `bench_mult` sim substeps per displayed frame (1..5). Bump it until // FPS drops below the refresh cap (frame time past vsync => compute-bound), // then ms/substep is the real, vsync-independent throughput figure to // compare before/after a change. ms_frame is the EMA of the whole frame. bench_mult: u32 = 3, ms_frame: f32 = 0, // Collapsing-section open state (closed by default - clean main view). show_advanced: bool = false, show_diag: bool = false, // The whole control panel is collapsed by default: just a small menu toggle // floats in the corner so the fluid is unobstructed until you want a knob. panel_open: bool = false, }; fn deinit(gpa: Allocator, s: *State) void { s.pipe.deinit(); s.cpu_pipe.deinit(); s.discs.deinit(); s.ui_host.deinit(); gpa.free(s.scratch); gpa.free(s.prev_stat_pos); z.unloadFont(gpa, s.font); } /// Spawn the initial state: a packed disk at domain centre, jittered so the /// columns don't lock, plus a small deterministic per-particle kick. Uploaded /// straight into the compute buffers; gravity does the rest. reset() re-runs it. fn spawnDamBreak(pipe: *z.Compute(fk), scratch: []Vec2) void { var prng: std.Random.DefaultPrng = std.Random.DefaultPrng.init(0xf1a1d); const rng: std.Random = prng.random(); var i: u32 = 0; while (i < fk.num_particles) : (i += 1) { const ang: f32 = rng.float(f32) * 6.2831853; const rad: f32 = 220.0 * @sqrt(rng.float(f32)); scratch[i] = .{ fk.domain_w * 0.5 + @cos(ang) * rad, fk.domain_h * 0.5 + @sin(ang) * rad, }; } pipe.upload(.pos, scratch[0..fk.num_particles]); @memcpy(fk.g.B.pos[0..fk.num_particles], scratch[0..fk.num_particles]); for (scratch[0..fk.num_particles], 0..) |*v, vi| { // small deterministic per-particle kick so motion reads on screen const a: f32 = float(vi % 628) * 0.01; v.* = .{ @cos(a) * 2.0, @sin(a) * 1.0 }; } pipe.upload(.vel, scratch[0..fk.num_particles]); @memcpy(fk.g.B.vel[0..fk.num_particles], scratch[0..fk.num_particles]); pipe.upload(.delta, scratch[0..fk.num_particles]); // Seed density bright so the colour reach-in renders before the first pass. for (scratch[0..fk.num_particles]) |*v| { v.* = .{ 600.0, 1.0 }; } pipe.upload(.density, scratch[0..fk.num_particles]); } fn initState(gpa: Allocator, f: *z.Frame, s: *State) !void { const font: z.Font = try z.loadFont(f, gpa, atkinson_mono_ttf, 24); var pipe: z.Compute(fk) = try z.Compute(fk).initGpu( gpa, f.gpu.device, f.gpu.queue, &kernel_wgsls, ); // Variable-length fields slice to this many elements on readback (the live // particle count). Dispatch widths are passed per call to `run(name, n)`; // this field is ONLY the readback length, set once here. pipe.element_count = fk.num_particles; const scratch: []Vec2 = try gpa.alloc(Vec2, fk.num_particles); const prev_stat_pos: []Vec2 = try gpa.alloc(Vec2, fk.num_particles); @memset(prev_stat_pos, .{ 0, 0 }); var cpu_pipe: z.Compute(fk) = z.Compute(fk).initCpu(); cpu_pipe.element_count = fk.num_particles; spawnDamBreak(&pipe, scratch); spawnDamBreak(&cpu_pipe, scratch); const n_bytes: u64 = fk.num_particles * 8; const discs: z.FluidDiscs = try z.FluidDiscs.init( f.gpu, gpa, f.gpu.device, f.gpu.queue, f.gpu.backbuffer_format, f.gpu.depth_format orelse .undefined_, .{ .handle = pipe.fieldBuffer(.pos).?, .size = n_bytes }, .{ .handle = pipe.fieldBuffer(.density).?, .size = n_bytes }, fk.domain_w, fk.domain_h, ); s.* = .{ .font = font, .pipe = pipe, .cpu_pipe = cpu_pipe, .discs = discs, .ui_host = z.UiHost.init(gpa, font), .scratch = scratch, .prev_stat_pos = prev_stat_pos, }; } fn update(f: *z.Frame, s: *State) void { // ---- Average-FPS benchmark (the baseline figure we're trying to beat) ---- // dt is the real frame delta; guard the first frame / pauses where it's 0. const dt: f32 = f.time.delta_time; if (dt > 0.0) { const inst_ms: f32 = dt * 1000.0; s.ms_frame = if (s.ms_frame == 0) inst_ms else s.ms_frame * 0.9 + inst_ms * 0.1; // Windowed average: accumulate frames, publish every fps_window_secs so // the headline number stays stable while you read it. s.fps_accum_time += dt; s.fps_accum_frames += 1; const fps_window_secs: f32 = 0.5; if (s.fps_accum_time >= fps_window_secs) { s.fps_avg = float(s.fps_accum_frames) / s.fps_accum_time; s.fps_accum_time = 0; s.fps_accum_frames = 0; } } // ---- Input -> mouse force (logical px -> sim px via the renderer's fit) ---- const lw: f32 = f.window.widthf(); const lh: f32 = f.window.heightf(); const mraw: Vec2 = z.getMousePosition(f.input); const mp_arr: [2]f32 = s.discs.simFromLogical(lw, lh, .{ mraw[0], mraw[1] }); const mp: Vec2 = .{ mp_arr[0], mp_arr[1] }; const pressing: bool = z.isMouseButtonDown(f.input, .left); const attract: bool = s.attract_toggle or z.isKeyDown(f.input, .left_shift) or z.isKeyDown(f.input, .right_shift); const signed_force: f32 = if (!pressing) 0.0 else if (attract) -s.mouse_force_mag else s.mouse_force_mag; // ---- Gravity: ONE effective-gravity vector from the phone (Einstein) ---- // getDeviceGravity returns -(proper acceleration) in canvas m/s^2: it already // contains gravity AND motion, so tilt, shake, flat-float and free-fall all // come from this single vector. g_force scales m/s^2 -> sim units. With phone // gravity off it returns plain (0, 9.8), i.e. classic straight-down gravity. const eff_g: Vec2 = if (s.phone_gravity) z.getDeviceGravity(f.input) else Vec2{ 0, 9.8 }; const accel_vec: Vec2 = eff_g * splat2(s.g_force); s.dbg_gravity = accel_vec; // ---- Substeps: 11 dispatches each, all on-device ---- // Compute this frame's sim params ONCE, before opening the batch: a batch // writes the uniform a single time at beginBatch, so params must be final by // then (endBatch asserts they don't change mid-batch). The same values drive // the one-time priming sort and every substep below. const live_count: u32 = @trunc(clamp(s.sim_count_f, 1, float(fk.num_particles))); const sim_params: fk.Params = .{ // THE LIVE COUNT, not the buffer capacity. This used to be `fk.num_particles`, so // the count slider changed only how many discs were DRAWN while the sim always ran // all 20000 - and because the counting sort orders particles by cell // (`cell = cx + cy*n_cols`), the first N slots are the particles in the LOWEST cell // ids, i.e. the TOP ROWS of the domain. Asking for 1000 particles therefore rendered // a thin band along the ceiling: a spatial slice, not a subset. In `fluid_gpu` there // is no reorder, so the same mistake looked harmless. .count = live_count, .dt = 1.0, .h = fk.interact_radius, .r0 = s.rest_density, .k_far = s.k_far, .k_near = s.k_near, .gravity_x = accel_vec[0], .gravity_y = accel_vec[1], .visc_beta = s.visc_beta, .mouse_x = mp[0], .mouse_y = mp[1], .mouse_force = signed_force, .mouse_radius = mouse_radius, .dom_w = fk.domain_w, .dom_h = fk.domain_h, .n_cols = fk.grid_cols, .n_rows = fk.grid_rows, .wall_normal_damp = s.wall_normal_damp, .wall_tangent_damp = s.wall_tangent_damp, }; // ONE pointer decides which backend the whole substep loop runs on. Everything below // dispatches through `pipe`, so the CPU and GPU paths cannot drift apart. const pipe: *z.Compute(fk) = if (s.cpu_sim) &s.cpu_pipe else &s.pipe; pipe.params = sim_params; // non-batch mode reads this per dispatch // Echo the uniform back out of the shader every frame, so the panel can prove - not // assume - that what the host wrote is what the kernel reads. pipe.run("paramEcho", 1); if (!s.paused and s.batch_mode and !s.cpu_sim) { pipe.beginBatch(sim_params); } var step: u32 = 0; s.frame_no += 1; // The benchmark multiplier scales the substep count at runtime so we can // push the GPU past the vsync cap and read a real ms/substep number. const bench_n: u32 = clamp(s.bench_mult, @as(u32, 1), @as(u32, 5)); if (!s.paused and !s.sort_primed) { // Prime the counting sort once: build cell_start + reorder the spawn // layout so the very first substep's viscosity (which runs BEFORE that // substep's own rebuild) reads a valid grid, not an uninitialised one. pipe.run("clearGrid", fk.grid_cells); pipe.run("countGrid", live_count); pipe.run("prefixSum", 1); pipe.run("scatter", live_count); pipe.run("copyback", live_count); s.sort_primed = true; } while (!s.paused and step < substeps * bench_n) : (step += 1) { // Clavet ordering: gravity+mouse -> viscosity -> predict, as three // dispatches. Viscosity runs on the STALE grid still in the buffer from // last frame's build (a damping term tolerates the drift), BEFORE predict // and BEFORE the rebuild - so the grid is still built only ONCE per frame // (below, on the predicted positions density+force need). Applying // viscosity pre-predict (rather than fused into force) is more stable, // which lets dt grow. if (s.en_gravity) { pipe.run("gravityMouse", live_count); } if (s.en_viscosity) { pipe.run("viscosity", live_count); } if (s.en_predict) { pipe.run("predict", live_count); } if (s.en_grid) { // Spatial counting sort: clearGrid (per cell) -> countGrid (per // particle) -> prefixSum (ONE invocation) -> scatter -> copyback. After // this pos/vel/prev are in CELL ORDER, so each cell's particles occupy // the contiguous range [cell_start[c], cell_start[c+1]) and the // neighbour passes read coalesced. grid_counts is reused as the // per-cell scatter cursor (prefixSum zeroes it after the scan). pipe.run("clearGrid", fk.grid_cells); pipe.run("countGrid", live_count); pipe.run("prefixSum", 1); pipe.run("scatter", live_count); pipe.run("copyback", live_count); } if (s.en_density) { pipe.run("density", live_count); } if (s.en_force) { pipe.run("force", live_count); } if (s.en_apply) { pipe.run("applyAndFinalize", live_count); } } if (!s.paused and s.batch_mode and !s.cpu_sim) { pipe.endBatch(); } // The discs bind GPU buffers, so a CPU-run sim has to be mirrored across before it can // be drawn. `readLatest` on `.cpu` is a direct read of the module globals - free. if (s.cpu_sim) { if (s.cpu_pipe.readLatest(.pos)) |p| { s.pipe.upload(.pos, p); } if (s.cpu_pipe.readLatest(.density)) |d| { s.pipe.upload(.density, d); } } // ---- Diagnostics readback (centroid/bbox/rho/frozen) - GATED + THROTTLED. // readLatest() copies EVERY GPU buffer to staging + submits + maps (a // blocking GPU sync), and the CPU scans 20k elements. Doing all THREE // readbacks every frame (for stats only visible in the `diagnostics` panel) // pinned the GPU and - critically - added ~3 GPU stalls/frame that inflate // ms_frame and distort the ms/sub reading. So only pay for it when the panel // is open AND only once every `diag_every` frames; the stat_* fields persist // between samples, so the panel still updates (~1x/sec) without taxing every // frame. Measure perf with the panel CLOSED for the cleanest number. // The probe: unconditional, throttled. One readback every 30 frames is cheap and it // answers the only question that matters right now. if (s.frame_no % 30 == 0) { if (pipe.readLatest(.pos)) |pos_now| { var mn: Vec2 = .{ 1e30, 1e30 }; var mx: Vec2 = .{ -1e30, -1e30 }; var nan_n: u32 = 0; for (pos_now) |p| { if (p[0] != p[0] or p[1] != p[1]) { nan_n += 1; continue; } mn = @min(mn, p); mx = @max(mx, p); } s.probe_p0 = pos_now[0]; s.probe_pos1 = pos_now[1]; s.probe_min = mn; s.probe_max = mx; s.probe_nan = nan_n; } if (pipe.readLatest(.grid_counts)) |gc| { for (0..4) |i| { s.probe_gc[i] = gc[i]; } } if (pipe.readLatest(.cell_start)) |cs| { for (0..4) |i| { s.probe_cs[i] = cs[i]; } } if (pipe.readLatest(.density)) |d| { s.probe_den = d[0]; } if (pipe.readLatest(.scratch)) |sc| { s.probe_pos2 = sc[0]; // WHAT THE SHADER ACTUALLY SEES, field by field, against what the host sent. const b: usize = fk.echo_base; fh = c2.host; fg = c2.gpu; } bad += 1; } } s.param_bad = bad; s.param_first = first; s.param_host = fh; s.param_gpu = fg; } } } const diag_every: u32 = 30; if (s.show_diag and s.frame_no % diag_every == 0) { if (pipe.readLatest(.pos)) |pos_all| { const pos_now: []const Vec2 = pos_all[0..@min(live_count, pos_all.len)]; var frozen: u32 = 0; for (pos_now, 0..) |p, i| { const dp: Vec2 = p - s.prev_stat_pos[i]; if (@abs(dp[0]) + @abs(dp[1]) < 0.01) { frozen += 1; } s.prev_stat_pos[i] = p; } s.stat_frozen_pct = 100.0 * float(frozen) / float(live_count);
